- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then overshoot, followed by a sharp drop — suggest smoothing or dampening of short-term spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly after mid-range values — may indicate failure to capture long-term mean reversion or delayed trend reversal.
- When true values show a sharp downward trend (e.g., after 70+), model often fails to adjust downward quickly — suggest adding a lagged trend correction or momentum filter.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is below 70 — may require dynamic scaling or adaptive baseline adjustment.
- Forecasts often fail to account for sudden drops in the final 5–7 days — may need a “tail risk” or “drop-off” penalty in the model.
